cachekey.copied: {noun} copied to the clipboard (not shown). smith reads it from {variable}: set that variable on this machine, and as a secret variable in your CI (`smith cache setup` shows the steps for each provider).
cachekey.copied.plain: {noun} copied to the clipboard (not shown). Paste it where you need it.
cachekey.env.windows.intro: This sets {variable} for your user on this machine:
cachekey.env.windows.done: {variable} is set for your user. New terminals pick it up. Terminals that are already open do not. To remove it, run: smith cache key --remove
cachekey.profile.intro: smith will add {variable} to {path}. These are the exact lines, with the secret hidden:
cachekey.profile.warning: Warning: backups of your dotfiles and dotfile git repositories keep the secret.
cachekey.profile.choices: Enter writes it   Esc cancels   h shows how to do it by hand
cachekey.profile.written: smith wrote {variable} to {path}. Open a new terminal to use it. Terminals that are already open do not have it. To remove it, run: smith cache key --remove
cachekey.profile.unsafe: The secret has characters that a shell line cannot hold safely. Nothing was written.
cachekey.byhand.file: To do it by hand, add this line to {path}, with your secret in place of <the key>:
cachekey.byhand.other: smith does not know a profile file for your shell. To do it by hand, add this line to the profile of your shell, with your secret in place of <the key>:
cachekey.byhand.next: Then open a new terminal. smith changed nothing.
cachekey.remove.windows: {variable} is no longer set for your user. Terminals that are already open keep it until they close.
cachekey.remove.none: smith found no secret that it set. Nothing changed.
cachekey.sas.expiry.login: Azure limits a token signed in as you to 7 days, so 7 days is the only choice. For a longer token (30, 90 or 365 days), go back and sign with the account key. A weekly expiry means renewing the CI secret every week.
cachekey.sas.expiry.other: How long should it last? You must renew it before it ends.
cachekey.sas.back.hint: choose how the token is signed again
